sentences.text: Caiuajara was an extinct genus of tapejarid pterosaur that lived in what is now Brazil.
The genus is known from a single species, Caiuajara dobruskii, which was named and described by Manzig et al. in 2014.
Adults possessed a large toothless head featuring an enormous crest resembling a shark fin over their snout.
The tip of the snout pointed downward at angles of 142 to 149 degrees relative to the upper jaw edge.
The largest individuals had an estimated wingspan of 2.35 meters.
This species represents the first pterosaur fossil discovered in southern Brazil.
In 2014, it was considered the geologically youngest known tapejarid and the most southern one known.
The snout crest grew significantly taller and steeper during development, changing inclination from about 115 degrees to 90 degrees.
Pterosaur fossils were discovered in 1971 by laborers Alexandre Dobruski and his son João Gustavo Dobruski near Cruzeiro do Oeste in the state of Paraná, Brazil.
Caiuajara lived in a desert environment featuring dunes.
No fossil plants have been found, so there are no direct indicators of its food source, though tapejarids are generally believed to be herbivores.
Large fossil concentrations suggest Caiuajara lived in colonies, indicating a gregarious lifestyle.
The predominance of juvenile fossils suggests possible creching behavior where young formed groups separate from adults, perhaps at a nursery site near an inland lake.
Evidence suggests Caiuajara were precocial, capable of flight shortly after hatching, implying limited parental care.
Histological analysis shows Caiuajara had a rapid growth rate with higher bone deposition rates than Rhamphorhynchus and Pterodaustro.
Caiuajara maintained a high metabolism throughout its life, unlike Rhamphorhynchus and Pterodaustro which developed lower metabolisms with age.
A study by Araújo et al. (2026) suggests Caiuajara dobruskii had metabolic rates intermediate between modern ectotherms and endotherms and was likely capable of prolonged powered flight.
The absence of crestless specimens indicates Caiuajara was not sexually dimorphic regarding the crest, challenging the hypothesis that pterosaurs were normally sexually dimorphic.
Caiuajara is classified within the family Tapejaridae, specifically the subfamily Tapejarinae.
A 2019 phylogenetic analysis placed Caiuajara within the tribe Tapejarini as a sister taxon to a group containing Europejara, Tapejara, and Tupandactylus.
The genus name refers to the Caiuá geological formation and the related genus Tapejara.
Caiuajara lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
The fossil record for Caiuajara spans from the Aptian to the Campanian stages, between 121.4 and 72.2 million years ago.
It is debated whether Caiuajara was herbivorous, as no fossil plants have been found associated with the fossils despite tapejarids often being assumed to be herbivores.
It is debated whether mass mortality was caused by storms or droughts.
